note: Per-dependency x per-platform pins for the rn-media engine. Measured from the two forks on 2026-08-11:
`fetch` records HOW the fork actually acquires the source. 'tarball' means url+sha256 is what the build
consumes. 'git-tag' means the fork runs `git clone --depth 1 --branch <ref>` and verifies NOTHING: the
url+sha256 recorded there is the equivalent release tarball, measured by the workshop, and it is a
reference value rather than a build input until the Android fork is moved onto checksummed tarballs.
That gap is declared as the repo-level 'source-integrity' divergence below; it is a bug, not a choice.
Every difference between the two platforms MUST be declared in the dependency's `divergence` field.
`workshop verify` fails on an undeclared divergence AND on a declared one that is no longer real.

repoDivergences.ref: rn-media task #32; found by `workshop verify-artifacts` against v0.7.2-rnmedia.5
repoDivergences.reason: The iOS SIMULATOR slice of Mpv.xcframework is built with every audio output disabled, so libmpv cannot play audio in the Simulator. The device slice (ios-arm64) is correct. Proven by the shipped binary's own embedded meson line: `-Daudiounit=disabled -Davfoundation=disabled -Daudiotrack=disabled -Daaudio=disabled -Dcoreaudio=disabled -Dopensles=disabled`. Cause: nix/packages/mk-pkg-mpv/default.nix gates IOS_OPTIONS (-Daudiounit=enabled) on `os == oses.ios`, but the simulator builds under a THIRD os value, oses.iossimulator, so it matches neither the macos nor the ios branch and falls through to DISABLE_ALL_OPTIONS. The same repo already handles this correctly in mk-out-frameworks/default.nix:83 (`[ $os == $oses.ios ] || [ $os == $oses.iossimulator ]`), so the fix is to use that idiom in the mpv derivation too. Parity impact: Android's x86/x86_64 EMULATOR ABIs do carry audiotrack, so audio works in the Android emulator and not in the iOS Simulator — a developer-facing parity gap under CLAUDE.md. Patch 007-mpv-audiounit-shared-session is also absent from that slice as a consequence, because ao_audiounit.m is never compiled into it.
repoDivergences.fix: LANDED on libmpv-darwin-build@rn-media-hls as ff0fb7005dd6ccc1e367a325c68fe4dbe5d90695 — nix/packages/mk-pkg-mpv/default.nix now tests `os == ios || os == iossimulator`, the same idiom mk-out-frameworks/default.nix:83 already used. One line of behaviour, no tag, no release. Darwin CI green on that sha (run 31524321963), and its build log shows `audiounit : enabled` for all three Apple targets including both simulator ones, where before it was disabled. It ships with the next darwin release (rn-media task #32, the parity release). Until that release exists, `workshop verify-artifacts --darwin-tag v0.7.2-rnmedia.5` STAYS RED by design: that tag was built before the fix and the check reports what SHIPPED, not what is fixed in source. Do not loosen it; re-run against the new tag.
repoDivergences.expectedAfterFix: MEASURED, not predicted — the CI artifact from run 31524321963 was downloaded and probed directly. On the darwin/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/Mpv slice: `audio-output` flips to PASS (the `audiounit` AO string is present, twice — once per arch of the fat binary — and none of avfoundation/coreaudio/audiotrack/aaudio/opensles is built in), and `patch-markers` flips to PASS (007-mpv-audiounit-shared-session's `skip-session-management` and `audio session users` both appear, because ao_audiounit.m is compiled into that slice for the FIRST time). Its embedded meson line now reads -Daudiounit=enabled. SIZE: the simulator slice grows 5,527,008 -> 5,548,256 bytes (+21,248 B, +0.38%), which is the AO and its Objective-C implementation entering the binary twice over — that is the fix landing and must NOT be read as a size regression. The DEVICE slice is byte-for-byte the same size (2,676,128 B before and after), which is the regression signal that the change touched only the simulator path.
repoDivergences.statusNote: Deliberately still `bug`. The fix is in source (ff0fb70) but no release carries it yet, and this manifest tracks what SHIPS. It moves to resolvedDivergences once a release built after that commit exists and `workshop verify-artifacts` is green against it.

Built STATIC into libmpv.so: no new DT_NEEDED, no new file to ship. LGPL-2.1-or-later, same as the artifact. NOTE it is fetched as a checksummed tarball rather than a git clone by tag -- the shape the rest of this fork's dependencies should move to.

divergence.reason: Android-only because Apple's libc already provides iconv and bionic does not until API 28. This is the two platforms reaching the SAME capability by different routes, which is the opposite of a divergence in behaviour: without it, iOS had working charset conversion and Android did not.

resolvedDivergences.note: The manifests treat parity as the ABSENCE of a divergence entry -- `workshop verify` fails on a declared divergence that is no longer measured -- so the entry is deleted rather than flipped to a "resolved" status. This list is the record.

resolvedDivergences.resolvedBy: rn-media task #32 (parity release): --enable-libxml2 and the libxml2 dependency itself removed from the Android fork.
resolvedDivergences.note: Nothing was lost. FFmpeg uses libxml2 only for the DASH demuxer and neither fork enables it, so the Android artifact was carrying an XML parser that no code path could reach. Both audio artifacts now agree: no libxml2, no DASH.

resolvedDivergences.was: flag/bug — Android named 27 mpv options and left ~95 at mpv's `auto` defaults
resolvedDivergences.resolvedBy: rn-media task #32 (parity release): Android now passes the same exhaustive list darwin does.
resolvedDivergences.note: 103 options on each side, 101 identical. The only two that differ are the platform audio output (audiotrack vs audiounit). No mpv feature can now enter either build by defaulting to `auto` -- the hazard that silently built a second AO into the darwin engine in 0.41.

resolvedDivergences.was: repo/bug — the Android fork fetched every source as a shallow clone of a MUTABLE TAG and verified nothing, while darwin carried a sha256 on all 22 of its sources
resolvedDivergences.resolvedBy: rn-media task #32 (parity release): every Android source is verified after fetching. Git clones assert the expected COMMIT (content-addressed, so re-pointing a tag cannot change what a SHA resolves to); libiconv, the one real tarball, is checked with sha256sum -c.
resolvedDivergences.note: Commit assertion rather than a switch to tarballs, deliberately: libplacebo needs five submodules and release tarballs ship those directories EMPTY, so tarballs would have broken the build to fix the provenance. media-kit-android-helper was additionally pinned from the moving `main` branch to a commit -- two builds a week apart could previously package different helper code with no version change anywhere.
